build: D64 disk image (disk name WWW.C64HQ.COM) of a Trilogic V2.9 crack: one 46,944-byte program that unpacks a frozen machine state, started at the title screen

exclude: Sprite pages of the first buffer: each frame's figures are built here from their parts every frame
First buffer's screen: the bitmap's colours, filled for the play area at each change of street part, and its sprite pointers
First buffer's bitmap: the street is redrawn here every frame; the frame and panel around it are the same picture as the second bitmap's, copied there by the cold start
Sprite pages of the second buffer, built every frame
Second buffer's screen: the bitmap's colours and its sprite pointers
Second buffer's bitmap: the street is redrawn here every frame, around it the frame and panel picture, which the Graphics page shows

Redraws the whole 36-character street view into the hidden bitmap from the street map, once a frame: 19 tile columns of 16 pixels, right to left, with half a tile at each edge when the scroll column is odd. The column number at $0DAE/$0DAF, halved, picks the first map byte; every operand of the copy at $03E7 is then written for it

The map byte for the view's left edge is $2B66 plus half the column number; written as the operand of the LDA at $031F, so that LDA $325B,Y with Y from 18 down reads the 19 map bytes from the right edge leftwards. The low bit of the column, kept with PHP, says the view starts half-way through a tile
Bit 0 of $DD00 says which buffer is hidden: its bitmap starts at $A000 or $E000, and the street's top-right tile lands at $A260 or $E260 (character row 1, column 36)
Writes the 16 destination addresses of the copy loop, one character row (320 bytes) apart

For each tile column, Y from 18 down to 0: the map byte is the tile number n, and the tile's graphics start at $326E + (n-1) x 256, 16 bytes to each of its 16 character rows; those 16 source addresses go into the copy loop
The operand of the LDA at $031F, low byte: the map byte at the view's left edge, so that Y from 18 down to 0 reads the view's 19 tile columns from right to left; written at $022D
The map address's high byte, written at $0230
The operand of the ADC at $032B: 0, or 8 for the half tile at the view's left edge, which starts half-way into the tile
Copies one tile column: 16 (or 8) bytes from each of the tile's 16 character rows to the 16 rows of the hidden bitmap. All 32 addresses are operands rewritten by $0221 and $031D

The frame update, run once a game loop. Works out the column at the left of the screen from the scroll position, redraws the street view, rebuilds the multiplexer tables for the hidden buffer, draws the three heroes' frames, waits for raster line $B2, draws the enemy's frame with the I/O area switched out (its graphics live under it), sets the sprite X positions, recolours the play area when a new part of the street begins, draws the items and shots into the bitmap ($283B), then shows the buffer just drawn
Waits for raster line $B2 before drawing the enemy's frame
The enemy's graphics are in the RAM under the I/O area, so the processor port is set to $30 (all RAM) for the copy, with interrupts off
Sprite enable bits ($0DB2) and X positions: each object is two sprites side by side, 24 pixels apart, with bit 8 of X from $0DA5
Which part of the street the scroll is in: 0 before $4A60, then 1, 2 and 3 after $24E0 and $03A0 (the street runs right to left, so the scroll position falls)
The CPY operand at $0A4D holds the part last coloured; nothing is redrawn while it matches
The CPY operand: the part of the street last coloured, written when a new part is coloured
A new part of the street: fills the screens and colour memory of the play area with that part's colours from $01E9 and $01ED
Flips bit 0 of $DD00, which selects the VIC-II bank, so the buffer just drawn is shown and the other is drawn next
Takes the new IRQ vector for the shown buffer from the pair of tables at $0165 and $0167
Three bytes no instruction names, before the first shape

The bitmap shapes that $283B draws straight into the screen: the street hazard's eight frames, the shots and the bonuses, 19 shapes in all, each a block of bitmap bytes some character rows high. $2810 says where each starts (two lie in the panel's spare bytes at $BF40 and $BFA0), $27EA how wide and $27FD how many rows
Jump to the cold start at $1024. Nothing in memory calls it: the original loader must have, and in this crack the frozen machine starts later, at the title
Jump to $1E29, which draws the enemy's frame; called from the display update at $09EC with the RAM under the I/O area switched in
Jump to $1E05, which draws one hero's frame (X = 0 to 2); called from the display update for each hero

Each sprite object's Y, which the multiplexer sorts
No instruction names this byte; it sits between the object tables and the scroll position

The game's own start, which never runs in this copy (the freezer saved the machine after it). One game frame. Reads the controls, moves the active hero and the two who follow, runs the enemy, tests the heroes' blows and the enemy's, updates the energy bars, decides which sprites are on, redraws the display, adds points, plays the sound, places the bonus items, and swaps the screen buffers

$1EE2 = 3: all three heroes are dead; $1EE2 = 4: the prize was taken. Both draw GAME OVER over the panel; the win then plays the jingle, the loss one sound, and both start a new game, which waits for fire
